title: Size and quantity
note: Too much: plethora, surfeit, glut, profusion. Too little: dearth, pittance, exiguous, scant. Tiny amounts: iota (the smallest Greek letter), scintilla (Latin for spark), modicum. Lilliputian comes from the tiny people of Gulliver's Travels; gargantuan from Rabelais's giant Gargantua.

items.ex: The reef shelters myriad species of fish.
The menu offered a plethora of choices and no clear specialty.

items.a: an excess, especially one that brings disgust
d: a lack of what is needed
items.ex: After a surfeit of holiday candy, even chocolate lost its charm.

items.a: an oversupply, especially of goods on a market
items.ex: A glut of tomatoes drove prices below the cost of picking them.
The dearth of affordable housing pushed young families out of town.
With a modicum of planning, the trip would have been easy.
The new evidence did not change the jury's mind one iota.
There was not a scintilla of proof that the dog ate the homework.

items.a: a slight, superficial knowledge or small amount
items.ex: He had a smattering of Italian, enough to order coffee and apologize.

items.a: a very small or inadequate amount of money
items.ex: Early sailors risked their lives for a pittance and a ration of biscuits.
She took copious notes, filling two notebooks in one lecture.

items.a: remarkably great in size, force, or degree
items.ex: The young pianist had a prodigious memory for scores.
The diner's gargantuan pancakes hung over the edge of the plate.
The retail behemoth opened a store the size of four football fields.
Beside the cruise ship, the fishing boats looked Lilliputian.
The diminutive goalkeeper stopped shots from players a foot taller.
The chance of two snowflakes matching exactly is infinitesimal.
The contract's key clause was printed in minuscule type.
In April the meadow erupts in a profusion of wildflowers.
The harvest festival celebrated the plenitude of the year.
Her multifarious duties ranged from payroll to plumbing.
The scholar lived on an exiguous stipend and a great deal of soup.
The witness paid scant attention to the car's color.

items.a: corresponding in size or degree; proportionate
items.ex: The job offers a salary commensurate with experience.
He spent an inordinate amount of time choosing a font.

items.a: a greater share in number, weight, or importance
items.ex: A preponderance of the evidence pointed to the brother.

items.a: a whole formed by combining parts; a total
items.ex: In the aggregate, small donations outweighed the big gifts.

items.a: very large in volume or extent
items.ex: The voluminous report ran to nine hundred pages.

items.a: having a lot of space inside; roomy
items.ex: Her capacious tote held a laptop, a lunch and a small umbrella.

items.a: an abundant supply of good things
items.ex: The farmers' market was a cornucopia of fruit and cheese.
